facts.text: When I was 5, I had an operation to remove a brain tumour from the right back part of my brain; it was an anaplastic astrocytoma.
After that operation I had radiation therapy to my brain: 3D conformal external-beam radiotherapy, 6000 cGy in 30 sessions.
My last brain MRI was when I was 15.
I've never had problems with headaches before.

aliases: earlier weakness or loss of function
facts.text: Before this I never had any neurological problems.

findings.name: neurological examination
findings.result: Visual testing: dense left homonymous hemianopia; the remainder of the neurological examination was normal.

findings.name: CT head without contrast
findings.result: Multiple cystic lesions, consistent with previous imaging.

findings.name: MRI brain with contrast
findings.result: Multiple periventricular and posterior subcortical cystic lesions with surrounding nonspecific T2 hyperintensity; T1-weighted post-contrast images show no enhancement.

findings.name: previous brain MRI
findings.result: Post-surgical changes and giant Virchow–Robin spaces, attributed to prior radiotherapy.

findings.name: vasculitis screen
findings.result: Antinuclear antibody positive at 1:160; extractable nuclear antigen negative; double-stranded DNA negative; p-ANCA negative; c-ANCA negative.

aliases: stroke-like migraine attacks after radiation therapy
stroke-like migraine attacks after radiation therapy syndrome
gold.reasoning: 1. SMART syndrome was considered given the triad of remote cranial irradiation, transient migraine-like headache, and focal neurologic deficit — “At this time, a provisional diagnosis of stroke-like migraine attacks after radiation therapy (SMART) syndrome was made, despite not having the classic radiological evidence to support it.” 2. Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome was unlikely in the absence of hypertension — “he had remained normotensive during the entirety of his admission.”

source_issues: The gold reasoning calls the headache transient, but the prompt gives only a 2-day history with no resolution.
notes: Index visit: the emergency presentation with 2 days of rapid-onset right retro-orbital headache and new difficulty navigating on the left (s001-s007); the day-3 MRI (s008) and the vasculitis screen (s009) are later findings from the same admission.
s001: the 2-day history covers both complaints, so it is one standalone duration fact (f005) rather than a child of either.

s006: 'the remainder of the neurologic and systemic examination was normal' is kept as a neurological examination record (with the hemianopia, so a full neurological examination request returns it) and a general examination record; the visual field record repeats the hemianopia for a targeted request.
s003: the age-15 MRI is a finding with time; the patient fact f008 only says he had it.
